newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends $4.25 lower, spreads get crushed.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends $4.25 lower, spreads get crushed.

text.p: LONDON, Jan 3 Reuter) - IPE gas oil futures ended $4.25 a tonne lower for January at $227.75 but above the days low of $226.75 set around midday.
Feb and March ended $3.50 and $2.25 lower respectively as intermonth spreads crumbled after bearish U.S. stock data.
Despite freezing weather across much of Europe, which helped lift prices earlier in the week, the mood among some technical traders was turning more bearish.
"Spread pressure was a signifcant feature today. Attempts to fill the (downside) gap were countered by a desire to buy the dips," said Tim holmes of brokers MeesPierson Derivatives.
Traders said most activity had centred on the Jan/Feb spread as the front month's expiry on January 10 drew closer. The spread ended at $5.00, some 75 cents below Thursday's close.
Brent fell to new lows after NYMEX opened despite steady demand for physical Brent and other Norwegian grades.
Feb was down 35 cents a barrel at $23.87 at 1743 GMT having held just below $24 for several hours in the middle of the day.
By dipping to $23.80 it managed to fill the downside gap left after Thursday's rally. Some dealers said that gap fill left the contract a better chance of recovering next week to higher levels.
Faltering gas oil and bearish American Petroleum Institute (API) stock data were cited as the main reasons for pushing Brent decisively below the psychologically important $24 level.

API data showed U.S. crude oil stocks held in primary storage rose 2.73 million barrels in the week ended December 27 to 295.60 million from 292.87 million, while distillates rose by 2.47 million barrels to 123.80 million from 121.33 million in the previous week.
